subject: Business
specVersion: Issue 2, February 2026 (stated in the PDF footer and cover); first teaching September 2017, first exam June 2019
statusNote: Official Pearson 4BS1 specification PDF (Issue 2, February 2026) downloaded and read as raw text (pdftotext). Paper structure, marks, weights, assessment objectives, all five content sections at numbered statement level (1.1.1 to 5.4.1), Appendix 2 command words, Appendix 3 quantitative skills and Appendix 4 formulae were compared line by line against that text. The 2027 qualification page was also opened for the 4BS1 last-assessment date. Statements are paraphrased. Year and term allocation is a recommended sequence, not a board requirement. Sample assessment materials were not opened.

sources.title: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE (9-1) Business 4BS1 specification (PDF)
Pearson International GCSE Business (2027) page (new qualification; confirms last assessment of 4BS1 is November 2028)

years: Years 10 to 11 (linear two-year course, all assessment at the end)

assessment.title: Investigating small businesses
assessment.content: Whole specification, set in the context of a small business (up to 49 employees, local or national market)
assessment.format: Four compulsory 20-mark questions mixing multiple choice, short answer, data response and open-ended writing; calculator allowed; June and November series; paper-based or onscreen; Level 1/2, single tier of entry; share of total marks by AO: AO1 13.7%, AO2 19.4%, AO3 11.3%, AO4 5.6%

assessment.title: Investigating large businesses
assessment.content: Whole specification, set in the context of a large business (more than 250 employees, multinational or global market)
assessment.format: Four compulsory 20-mark questions mixing multiple choice, short answer, data response and open-ended writing; calculator allowed; June and November series; paper-based or onscreen; Level 1/2, single tier of entry; share of total marks by AO: AO1 13.7%, AO2 19.4%, AO3 11.3%, AO4 5.6%

nonExam: None: 100% external written papers. Quantitative skills are 10% of total marks across both papers, always in a business context. Six ratio formulae are provided in the exam. Assessments use International Accounting Standards terms (for example statement of financial position, inventory).

aos.desc: Recall, select and communicate knowledge and understanding of business terms, concepts and issues
Apply knowledge and understanding using terms, concepts, theories and calculations in context
Select, organise and interpret business information from sources to investigate and analyse issues
Evaluate business information to make reasoned judgements and reach conclusions

units.title: Business objectives
points: 1.1.1 Financial aims: survival, profit, sales, market share, financial security
1.1.1 Non-financial aims: social objectives, personal satisfaction, challenge, independence, control
1.1.2 Aims and objectives change as the business evolves
1.1.2 Triggers: market conditions, technology, performance, legislation, internal reasons

units.title: Types of organisations
points: 1.2.1 Ownership types: sole trader, partnership, private and public limited company, public corporation
1.2.2 Compare forms by risk, ownership and limited liability
1.2.2 Reasons for and against public corporations being publicly owned
1.2.2 Compare control, sources of finance and use of profits
1.2.2 Stakeholders and shareholders; judge which ownership form suits a business
1.2.3 Other forms: franchises, social enterprises and multinationals

units.title: Classification of businesses
points: 1.3.1 Primary sector businesses extract raw materials
1.3.1 Secondary sector businesses convert raw materials into finished or semi-finished goods
1.3.1 Tertiary sector businesses provide a wide range of services

units.title: Decisions on location
points: 1.4.1 Location and relocation depend on proximity to market, labour, materials and competitors
1.4.1 The nature of the business activity affects the location
1.4.1 The internet: e-commerce and/or fixed premises
1.4.1 Legal controls and trade blocs influence location

units.title: Market research
points: 4.1.1 Purpose: find customer wants and needs, identify market gaps
4.1.1 Reduces risk and provides evidence for decisions
4.1.2 Primary methods: surveys, questionnaires, focus groups, observation, test marketing
4.1.2 Secondary sources: online sources, market reports, government reports
4.1.3 Qualitative and quantitative data
4.1.3 Role of social media in gathering data; why data must be dependable

units.title: The market
points: 4.2.1 Marketing meets customer requirements, builds relationships and retains loyal customers
4.2.1 Market orientation versus product orientation
4.2.1 Market share and its analysis
4.2.1 Niche versus mass marketing
4.2.2 Responding to shifting needs, spending patterns and increased competition
4.2.3 Segmentation by location, demographics, lifestyle, income and age

units.title: The marketing mix
points: 4.3.1 Product: developing a new product or service; goods versus services
4.3.1 Packaging and its importance
4.3.1 Product life cycle phases and extension strategies
4.3.1 Boston matrix for managing the product portfolio
4.3.2 Price: cost-plus, penetration, competition-based, skimming and promotional pricing, and when each suits
4.3.3 Place: distribution through retailers and e-tailers (e-commerce)
4.3.4 Promotion: advertising, sponsorship, product trials, special offers and branding for different segments
4.3.4 Above-the-line and below-the-line promotion; public relations
4.3.4 Technology in promotion: targeted online advertising, viral social media, e-newsletters; importance of a brand

units.title: Internal and external communication
points: 2.1.1 Why good communication matters and problems caused by poor communication
2.1.1 Communication methods, including IT, with their benefits and limitations
2.1.2 How barriers to communication arise
2.1.2 Problems from ineffective communication and how to remove barriers

units.title: Recruitment and selection process
points: 2.2.1 Employment types: full-time, part-time, job share, casual, seasonal, temporary
2.2.2 Documents: job description, person specification, application form, CV
2.2.3 Internal versus external recruitment, job advertisements, shortlisting and interviewing
2.2.4 Equal opportunities law: gender, race, disability, religion, sexual preference, age
2.2.4 Minimum wage law and its effects on businesses

units.title: Training
points: 2.3.1 Importance of training to the business and to workers
2.3.1 Training types and purposes: induction, on-the-job, off-the-job
2.3.1 Training and compliance with health and safety law
2.3.1 Benefits and limitations of training

units.title: Motivation and rewards
points: 2.4.1 Motivation attracts and retains employees and improves productivity
2.4.1 Motivation theories of Herzberg, Maslow and Taylor
2.4.2 Financial methods: remuneration, bonuses, commission, promotion, fringe benefits
2.4.2 Non-financial methods: job rotation, job enrichment, autonomy

units.title: Organisation structure and employees
points: 2.5.1 Organisational charts: hierarchical and flat structures
2.5.1 Centralised and decentralised structures
2.5.2 Roles and responsibilities: span of control, chain of command, delegation
2.5.3 Human resources: workforce planning, recruitment and selection, training, health and safety, staff welfare, employment issues, industrial relations
2.5.3 Human resources: disciplinary, grievance, dismissal, unfair dismissal, redundancy
2.5.3 Finance: wages and salaries, cash-flow forecasting, budgets, accounting
2.5.3 Marketing: research, product planning, pricing, sales promotion, advertising, customer service, PR, packaging, distribution
2.5.3 Production: manufacturing, designing new products, quality control, stock control

units.title: Business finance - sources
points: 3.1.1 Short-term and long-term finance needs
3.1.1 Finance to start up or expand a business
3.1.2 Internal sources: personal savings, retained profit, selling assets
3.1.3 External sources: overdrafts and trade payables
3.1.3 Loan capital and share capital, including stock market flotation for plcs
3.1.3 Venture capital and crowdfunding

units.title: Cash flow forecasting
points: 3.2.1 Cash pays suppliers, overheads and employees
3.2.1 Cash shortages can cause insolvency and failure
3.2.1 Cash and profit are different
3.2.2 Calculate and interpret cash inflows, outflows and net cash flow
3.2.2 Opening and closing cash balances

units.title: Costs and break-even analysis
points: 3.3.1 Revenue, fixed costs, variable costs and total costs
3.3.1 Profit and loss calculations
3.3.2 Break-even level of output from a formula or diagram
3.3.3 Effects of changes in revenue and costs on break-even charts
3.3.3 Limitations of break-even charts

units.title: Financial documents
points: 3.4.1 Statement of comprehensive income: sales, cost of sales, gross profit, expenses, operating profit
3.4.1 Use it in decision making; construction is not required
3.4.1 The nature and importance of profit
3.4.2 Statement of financial position: current and non-current assets and liabilities, capital employed
3.4.2 Interpret it; construction is not required

units.title: Accounts analysis
points: 3.5.1 Calculate and analyse gross profit margin and operating profit margin
3.5.1 Calculate and analyse markup and return on capital employed (ROCE)
3.5.1 Calculate and analyse current ratio and acid test ratio; formulae are supplied in the exam
3.5.2 Concept and importance of liquidity
3.5.2 Compare liquidity with earlier years and other businesses
3.5.3 Use financial documents to assess performance and inform decisions

units.title: Economies and diseconomies of scale
points: 5.1.1 Internal economies of scale: average total costs fall as output rises
5.1.1 External economies of scale: average total costs fall due to outside factors
5.1.2 Diseconomies of scale and limits to growth

units.title: Production
points: 5.2.1 Job, batch and flow production, and the impact of each
5.2.1 Labour-intensive and capital-intensive production
5.2.1 Calculate productivity and the effect of improving it
5.2.2 Lean production: just-in-time (JIT) and Kaizen
5.2.2 Using resources effectively
5.2.3 Impact of technology in production, including robotics
5.2.3 Balancing cost, productivity, quality and flexibility

units.title: Factors of production
points: 5.3.1 Changing relationships between enterprise, capital, land and labour
5.3.1 Capital-intensive versus labour-intensive activities

units.title: Quality
points: 5.4.1 Concept of quality and its importance for goods and services
5.4.1 Quality control and total quality management (TQM)
5.4.1 Using quality to gain competitive advantage

units.title: Business and the international economy
points: 1.5.1 Globalisation as a concept, with opportunities and threats for businesses
1.5.2 Growth of multinationals: benefits to the business
1.5.2 Benefits and possible drawbacks of multinationals to the host country or economy
1.5.3 Calculating exchange rates
1.5.4 Exchange rate changes affect international competitiveness, importers and exporters

units.title: Government objectives and policies
points: 1.6.1 Government spending on public services, taxation and constraints on spending
1.6.2 Government influence through infrastructure provision and legislation
1.6.2 Trade policy: trading bloc membership and tariffs
1.6.3 Interest rate effects on businesses and consumer spending

units.title: External factors
points: 1.7.1 Social factors affecting business decisions
1.7.1 Technological factors affecting business decisions
1.7.1 Environmental factors affecting business decisions
1.7.1 Political factors affecting business decisions

units.title: What makes a business successful?
points: 1.8.1 Measures: revenue, market share, customer satisfaction, profit and growth
1.8.1 Measures also include owner/shareholder satisfaction and employee satisfaction
1.8.2 Failure reasons: cash flow problems or lack of finance
1.8.2 Failure reasons: lack of competitiveness and failure to adapt to market changes

commandWords.meaning: Select one or more correct answers; recall or a calculation
Give the meaning of a term from the specification
Give an answer that tests recall of specification knowledge
Give an answer of up to a sentence, chosen from the context
Select the correct answer from a graph or table
Apply maths to given data and show working
Work out the missing values in a table
Give two linked points about a concept, placed in context
Make a statement with two expansion points; no context needed
Extended answer exploring a concept in context
Extended answer using given information to recommend one of two options
Extended answer using knowledge to reach a supported conclusion

skills: Quantitative skills are 10% of total marks in both papers, always in a business context, at upper-secondary maths level
Calculate percentages, percentage changes, averages, revenue, costs and profit
Calculate gross profit margin and net profit margin, and average rate of return
Calculate cash-flow forecasts, including total costs, total revenue and net cash flow
Interpret graphs, charts and profitability ratios (gross and net profit margin)
Interpret financial data (profit and loss, average rate of return, cash-flow forecasts), market research data and market data (share, cost and price changes)
Formulae supplied in the exam: gross profit margin, operating profit margin, markup, ROCE, current ratio, acid test ratio
Extended writing: analyse, justify and evaluate with a supported conclusion
Reading and writing English at roughly CEFR B2 level; desk calculator allowed, battery or solar only

prerequisites.from: KS3 Mathematics: percentages, averages and substitution

links.topic: Percentages, percentage change, averages and ratio
links.how: Maths supplies the methods; Business applies them to margins, ROCE and liquidity ratios
Break-even by formula and diagram uses linear graphs and algebra from Maths
Exchange rate calculations use ratio and proportion

links.topic: Persuasive writing, audience and branding language
links.how: Promotion and branding rely on persuasive language; English develops analysis of purpose and audience
Analyse, justify and evaluate answers need reasoned, supported conclusions

links.topic: E-commerce, digital communication and online marketing
links.how: Computing explains the technology; Business assesses its effect on place and promotion
Spreadsheet skills support building cash flow forecasts and break-even tables
Geography covers where and why production locates; Business covers the firm's decisions and effects on host countries
Geography provides environmental evidence; Business weighs it against cost and profit

links.topic: Lawful trade, honest dealing and the rules on interest (riba)
links.how: Sources of finance such as loans can be discussed alongside Islamic teaching on trade, kept factual and separate from the exam content

links.topic: Fair treatment of workers and ethical conduct
links.how: Motivation and rewards can be compared with Islamic teaching on fair pay and conduct; enrichment, not examined
Arabic First Language topic 7 uses work and employment themes that recruitment content supports
Science underpins robotics and production technology; Business evaluates cost, productivity and quality

contextNote: Both papers use real-style business contexts (small business in Paper 1, large or multinational in Paper 2). Teach the range of business viewpoints accurately and let pupils evaluate. Islamic perspectives in the links are enrichment and are not examined.
gaps: Sample assessment materials, mark schemes and examiner reports were not opened.
Entry for 4BS1 should be confirmed with the exams officer; the board states the last 4BS1 assessment is November 2028.
The school's lesson files were written to UK GCSE 1BS0 unit titles and need re-mapping to 4BS1.
Spec Appendix 3 names net profit margin and average rate of return, but Appendix 4 supplies no formulae for them.
